doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: Cannonball at Fredonia and how he got known in New York
summary: Rowe recalls playing before Cannonball at a Fredonia clinic; Parsons tells how Cannonball wailed on I Remember April at a New York jam and was known as a Florida teacher at Dillard High School.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: That’s terrific. I had to play – I forgot to mention that he came to Fredonia, SUNY Fredonia where I went to school up in New York State, and they came just like when they came to A&M. And they did a clinic and I had to play, I shouldn’t say I had to, I got to play in front of Cannonball. And the odd part was there was no rhythm section. So we
were just like playing a cappella. And I don’t remember what I did but he was pretty gracious especially I think it was like 9:00 in the morning you know.
Yeah. Do you know the story of how he got known in New York?
Yes I do. As a matter of fact Jerome Richardson told me that story but what do you know of it?

Well they were like okay who’s this fat boy from down there in the south, okay let’s get rid of him you know. So he said whatever it was, “I Remember April” might have been the tune and they took it way uptempo and took it through the keys on him. They thought they were going to get rid of him. But that’s his thing. So he wailed. And next thing it was all over town, here’s this boy from down there in Florida who’s killing it.
And wasn’t he a school teacher at the time?
Yeah, yeah. Dillard High School down in Ft. Lauderdale, down in South Florida.
